title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier with a bounded automated repair budget increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Each paired intent produced one shared_initial generation that was evaluated under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We archive preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment network changes, semantic correctness properties—sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—are operationally critical and cannot be assured by syntactic checks alone. A common engineering pattern is generate→validate→repair, where a deterministic validator checks candidate changes and a constrained repair operator attempts localized fixes. The measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends on (i) what is held fixed (the estimand), (ii) the single‑shot generator quality, (iii) validator expressiveness, and (iv) permitted repair budget.

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that isolates deterministic rescue by conditioning on a single shared LLM draw per intent. The primary research question asks: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair? Our contributions are: (1) an estimand‑explicit, preregistered paired evaluation isolating bounded deterministic rescue; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle (archived) that includes validator traces and the single automated repair transcript; and (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of ceiling effects, cost tradeoffs, and implications for NetOps CI/CD policies.
sections.related_work:
LLMs and tool‑augmented agents have been applied to NetOps and intent translation in numerous recent studies and surveys that document tasks, prototype systems, and practical tradeoffs [1–3]. Planner‑centric and ReAct‑style frameworks enable LLMs to call external validators, simulators, or synthesizers to coordinate multi‑step workflows; these architectures demonstrate that external tools can complement generative components but require careful tool design and integration [2,4]. Empirical reports indicate that deterministic checks and generate→validate→repair scaffolds often improve surface correctness relative to unconstrained generation, but absolute gains vary with validator coverage, task distribution, and whether pipelines permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration [3,1].

A related thread proposes semantic, verifier‑centric benchmarks emphasizing reachability, sequencing, and policy invariants rather than mere syntactic/template matching; community adoption of such benchmarks remains incomplete, limiting cross‑work comparisons [5,8]. Hybrid repair approaches combining symbolic fault‑localization or formal checks with generative repair operators show promise for configuration and program repair, but success depends on fault class and verifier expressiveness [6,3]. Work on hallucination detection and deterministic safety nets further highlights the dependence of mitigation effectiveness on the validator's semantic reach and the chosen threat model [7]. Our study explicitly narrows the estimand (shared_initial, single LLM draw) to measure bounded deterministic rescue separate from resampling or interactive strategies advocated in some prior work.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The confirmatory design was preregistered (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7). The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) computed on N = 300 paired intents following the preregistered inclusion/exclusion rules.

Task suite and stratification. A deterministic task generator produced a synthetic_topology_suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high). The confirmatory run sampled 100 paired intents per stratum; each pair encodes the natural‑language intent, initial and expected final states, sequencing constraints (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), and protected interfaces. This design ensures balanced per‑stratum representation and reproducible difficulty metadata.

Shared_initial protocol and model configuration. To isolate deterministic validator/repair rescue from resampling effects we used the shared_initial estimand: for each pair the system produced exactly one shared_initial candidate which was evaluated under both conditions. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json: requested_model = "gpt-5-mini"). The hosted adapter enforced a single shared_initial call per pair and permitted at most one repair invocation per guarded episode.

Validator and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation. The validator deterministically checks sequencing invariants, required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability encoded by the suite, and forbidden‑template protections. Scoring is binary (unflagged pass vs. flagged). The guarded pipeline allowed a single automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤ 1) implemented as a constrained localized edit routine limited to sequencing insertions or small localized command insertions; repaired candidates were deterministically re‑validated.

Execution auditing and accounting. The run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter under scientific_confirmatory mode. The preregistered planned_episode_count = 600; completed_episode_count = 600; complete_pair_count = 300. Provider/audit records show hosted_model_call_event_count = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair invocation) and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 300, repair: 1}. All execution and reconciliation checks passed deterministically.

Inference plan and CI choices. The confirmatory analysis used a paired binary test (exact two‑sided McNemar) on discordant counts (n10,n01) with a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000) to bound effect‑size uncertainty. The bootstrap percentile interval was chosen to provide an interpretable absolute paired difference bound when discordance is small and exact test power is limited; the bootstrap parameters were preregistered and archived. Sensitivity analyses (failure‑as‑zero, stratum‑wise exploratory tests with multiplicity control) were designated but treated as secondary.
sections.results:
Execution integrity and counts. The adapter completed 600 episodes producing 300 paired observations under the shared_initial protocol. No pairs were excluded; no provider/infrastructure dual‑call outages occurred. Model call accounting: model_calls_used = 301; repair_stage_count = 1.

Primary outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency counts are n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test yields p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. Because discordance is minimal (m = n10 + n01 = 1), the exact test has limited sensitivity; the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per stratum: low baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. The single discordant episode occurred in the high stratum and invoked the permitted automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial failure to a sequencing omission (an explicit 'admin down' step was missing); the constrained repair performed one localized insertion and the repaired candidate then passed deterministically. The repair therefore produced a deterministic rescue with one additional repair invocation; the repair provider trace and validator before/after summaries are archived as part of the run bundle.

Contamination and missingness. The preregistered contamination checks produced no contamination flags. The missingness summary reports zero failed or unscorable episodes and zero excluded pairs under the preregistered rules.
sections.discussion:
Estimand conditioning and operational alignment. The shared_initial estimand corresponds to operational policies that limit model calls (cost, latency, governance). Under these policies the guarded pipeline measures only bounded deterministic validator/repair rescue applied to the identical candidate. Alternative operational choices—allowing resampling, verifier‑guided regeneration, or iterative repair—change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates by exploiting generator variance; such workflows should be evaluated under different preregistered designs.

Ceiling effects and pilot omission. The preregistration included an optional pilot (n = 60) to estimate discordance and calibrate power; that pilot was not executed. As a result the baseline single‑shot performance was near ceiling (299/300), producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and limited power to detect small absolute improvements. This practical outcome underlines the value of small calibration pilots when generator performance may be high on chosen suites.

Validator scope and failure‑mode dependence. The single failure observed was a sequencing omission; other semantic failure modes (complex reachability violations, ACL semantics) were rare or absent in this synthetic suite. The marginal utility of a guarded pipeline therefore depends on (i) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (ii) the validator's expressiveness. Richer validators that detect broader reachability or policy semantics could increase observed rescue rates; conversely, operator policies that disallow automated edits constrain operational rescue to detection and human escalation.

Repair budget and cost tradeoffs. The guarded pipeline invoked one additional repair call across 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), showing that bounded deterministic repair can produce rescue at very low marginal model‑call cost in this run. Larger repair budgets or iterative repair strategies would likely raise rescue probability but increase model‑call and latency costs; practitioner decisions must balance these tradeoffs according to governance and cost constraints.

Implications for NetOps evaluation. Evaluations should align estimands with realistic operational policies: if pipelines permit multiple model calls, evaluations should allow resampling and interactive steering; if model calls are budgeted, the shared_initial estimand provides a conservative bound for deterministic rescue achievable by post‑hoc validation and bounded repair. Our archived artifacts (task manifests, validator traces, repair trace, and execution accounting) enable targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, validator expressiveness, model strength, and repair budget.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired comparison between a deterministic verifier + ≤1 automated repair pipeline and accepting a single LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued a single sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and targeted follow‑ups that vary estimand, model, or repair policy.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
